column3: Directly pairs the Lord's knowledge of straying from His سبيل with those rightly guided.
Contrasts steadfastness with following the سبيل of those without knowledge.
Keeps the shown سبيل open to divergent human responses, preserving agency within guidance.
Adds how a restricted knowledge-horizon can issue in losing the سبيل.
The immediately preceding contrast makes response to ease and harm disclose a formed human stance.
Shows guided paths enacted through reliance and endurance, rather than merely claimed.
Joins best conduct in calling with the Lord's exclusive knowledge of who leaves or follows the سبيل.
Adds that what people do is fully known and later reported, extending the focus's final discernment.
Shows a false moral claim issuing in unequal, concrete conduct toward others.
Presents taking a سبيل to the Lord as a voluntary response rather than an external reward.
Adorned deeds generate wandering, a mechanism by which formed practice obscures direction.
Uses شكل only for like kinds in another setting; it offers a limited lexical resonance.
Makes guidance depend on the fit between a person's bearing and a straight path.
Physical سبل provide a secondary model for orientation and guidance.
Adds that works lose weight when their underlying relation to the signs and return is broken.
Sets divine knowledge of created human interiority against self-purification claims.
Shows adorned practice blocking the سبيل and sustaining its own misdirection.
Links faith with صالح deeds, supporting action as an outward disclosure of a settled orientation.
Tests a claim of superior guidance by whether it yields a followable route.
Directly parallels working from one's موقف, with outcomes exposing the true stance.
As contrast evidence, it shows bad work in obstructing God's سبيل without resolving the focus's positive reading.
The refusal of payment and divine witness add no distinct disposition-to-action or path relation.
Creation and divine knowledge here do not add to the focus's action, form, or route relation.
Retains the voluntary taking of a سبيل but adds little beyond earlier route-choice cards.
Extends the nearby surah context with the Lord's encompassing knowledge of created ranks.
Shows that misguidance leaves no viable سبيل, an outcome of failed orientation.
Invalidated works add accountability context but no clear path or formed-character mechanism.
The visibility of even slight good acts is only a secondary accountability link.
A ruler's asserted سبيل of rightness supplies a contrary claim requiring discernment.
Affirms divine guidance's security but adds little about how action issues from disposition.
The visibility of slight evil acts is only a secondary accountability link.
Connects denial of guidance with the formed excess and lying of its subject.
Embodies severe path-loss as inverted movement and a bad destination.
Records a rival claim of superior guidance but supplies no further criterion for it.
Shows the later search for a return-path after misguidance has closed it.
Loss of works under association is relevant only as a general contrary outcome.
Links adorned plotting, accountable acquisition, and being turned from the سبيل.
Divine possession of knowledge supports the focus's final clause only in general terms.
Reiterates the Lord's discernment of leaving the سبيل and being guided.
Pairs believing صالح action with freedom from injustice, a secondary action-account link.
The Creator's knowing supports the focus's attribution of discernment to the Lord.
Following a messenger leading to guidance adds a general route relation already well established.
Tests a hypothetical claim to better guidance against the actual reception of signs.
Hostile hands and speech do not add a route or formed-action relation.
Contrasts a self-serving interior claim with later disclosure of what was done.
Attributes an adverse outcome to yourselves, connecting consequence to human source.
Names manifest misguidance but contributes no distinct formed-action mechanism.
Relates secure guidance to faith not mixed with ظلم.
The counterfactual route of alleged gods does not clarify human شاكلة or conduct.
Divine seeing of deeds determines final separation beyond family attachment.
Calls an inherited prohibited pattern a bad سبيل, a limited social-habit parallel.
Keeps wrongdoing attributable to the self and makes turning back a changed response.
The Lord's knowledge of what is in breasts directly grounds discernment beyond visible action.
A lasting physical road is only an external and historical path image.
The gap between sworn intent and rejecting response makes inner orientation visible in conduct.
Its ethical commitments specify conduct, but without a distinct path or disposition account.
Distinguishes service from striving in God's سبيل, a limited corrective to external appearance.
Shows a persistent preference for سبيل الغي over سبيل الرشد despite seeing both.
Rejection of signs closes the relation through which guidance is received.
The assertion of divine truth and power supplies no specific link to the focus.
The request for an exit-way after confession adds the irreversibility of a completed course.
Deviation from command appears, but the scene adds little to formed character and route assessment.
Frames guidance to the Lord as a transfer of the authority shaping conduct.
Returns each completed work to its agent under full divine knowledge.
Guided followers offer a secondary example of following rather than self-formed action.
Leaves the true أصحاب الصراط and guided party to a later disclosed distinction.
Exposes inherited traces as a self-confirming but untested claim to guidance.
Again stages work from one's station, though the earlier parallel already establishes it.
Invokes fighting in God's سبيل without adding a distinct disposition or route mechanism.
Divine dominion and protection do not develop the focus's action-path relation.
The nearby surah continuation links present inner blindness with deeper loss of the سبيل.
Defers disputed claims to the Lord's knowledge of actual deeds.
Names the Book as guidance but does not specify the focus's formed-action relation.
Joins the Lord's knowledge of brought guidance with the eventual outcome of a course.
Shows identical fighting ethically differentiated by the سبيل to which it is attached.
Makes good or evil work return upon the self before return to the Lord.
Distinguishes inducing path-loss from a group's own loss, preserving different responsibility readings.
Adds collective calling to records of what was done, but repeats the accountability dimension.
A false approach to God and withheld guidance offer only an indirect contrary route reading.
Reiterates the Lord's knowledge of guidance and manifest misguidance without a new mechanism.
Tests whether guidance persists when familiar outward cues are altered.
Divine knowledge differentiates persons in a judgment scene, only generally echoing the focus.
Relates exertion to divinely opened plural paths, while adding little beyond earlier path enactment.
The distinction of faith and doubt adds a general interior test, not a route of action.
Shows protective oaths becoming a sustained practice that blocks movement on God's سبيل.
Divine knowledge of contentious speech supplies only a broad accountability resonance.
Connects plural ways of peace with emergence to a straight path.
Shows each community's adorned view of its own work, then its correction through return and report.
Denies that reception of guidance is personal achievement, preserving its divine source.
Contrasts failed directed agency with justice-commanding uprightness on a straight path.
The description of woven couches has no material relation to the focus.
Makes obstructing God's سبيل rebound as the loss of direction for one's own works.
Names being upon guidance but does not develop the focus's disposition and action relation.
Subordinates communal names to faith and صالح action, a broad but already-covered measure.
The salutation adds no action, inner-form, knowledge, or path relation.
Affirms guidance and loss as divine outcomes but repeats an earlier general distinction.
Makes repentance insufficient at the end unless the prior lived direction has actually changed.
Sequences return, faith, صالح action, and guidance as restoration, extending the prior repentance card.
Tests what is concealed in breasts under conflict, connecting inward state with lived consequence.
Redirects dispute from claims to the Lord's knowledge of what opponents do.
Makes benefit and harm return upon the agents themselves, reinforcing that conduct discloses and carries a human course.
Directly states that guidance and misguidance accrue to the self, sharpening the focus's individual action-path relation.
Shows an inward preference for the immediate world issuing in a corresponding pursued course and outcome.
Sets seeking the later life, faith, and exertion together as a formed orientation expressed in action.
The Lord knows what is within selves, directly complementing 17:84's attribution of final discernment to Him.
Makes hearing, sight, and heart answerable for what a person pursues.
Turns an arrogant manner of walking into a visible limit on human self-conception.
The shift from distress to forgetfulness exposes a recurrent disposition through changing circumstances.
Names avarice as a human trait that governs conduct even under imagined abundance.
Directly parallels the command to work from one's مكانة and await whose outcome belongs to the abode.
Places created form before guidance, providing a close creation-and-direction counterpart to شاكلة and سبيل.
Links creation with proportioning, a foundational parallel for formed human configuration.
Links measured determination with guidance, directly extending the form-to-direction relation.
Centers the fashioned النفس as the relevant interior subject of divergent conduct.
Places opposing moral capacities within the formed النفس rather than in an undifferentiated exterior act.
Makes purification of the النفس the successful response to that interior moral condition.
Makes corruption of the النفس the contrary completed course.
Explicitly declares human striving diverse, a concise parallel to each working according to a distinct form.
Shows giving, reverence, and affirmation as a coherent action-pattern.
Shows the contrary action-pattern receiving a correspondingly difficult course.
Makes change in a people's condition contingent on change in what is in themselves.
Shows a person abandoning signs and following desire, joining interior orientation to misguiding action.
Develops the persistence of desire-led inclination as a contrary character-pattern.
Connects hearts, eyes, and ears not used for guidance with being more astray.
Depicts guidance and misguidance through expansion or constriction of the breast.
Pairs seeing for oneself with blindness against oneself, extending personal responsibility for orientation.
Shows hearts and sight turned as a result of persistent refusal, a contrary interior trajectory.
Contrasts the one straight path with proliferating paths that divide from it.
Names the intended course of the سبيل and a deviating alternative.
Sets worshipful alignment against false authority and distinguishes guided from misled peoples.
Joins divine guidance and misguidance with later questioning about what people did.
Contrasts an opened breast for submission with hardened hearts, making inward receptivity decisive for direction.
States that guidance and misguidance return upon the person, echoing the focus's individual course.
Makes following guidance or misguidance accrue to the self, with the messenger not controlling it.
Repeats personal consequence for guidance and misguidance in the setting of recitation and warning.
Preserves choice at the point of truth while retaining divergent consequences.
Directs attention to the self and distinguishes one's course from another's misguidance.
Attributes evil that reaches a person to the self, a direct responsibility counterpart to 17:84.
Makes earning evil an act against one's own self.
Treats departure from the believers' path as a chosen contrary route with consequence.
Makes righteous and evil action return upon the self, closely supporting action as self-implicating course.
Pairs disbelief and righteous action with distinct outcomes prepared by their agents.
Makes striving return to the striver's own benefit.
Limits a human being to what that person has striven for, reinforcing personal action-source.
Makes every النفس held by what it has earned.
Makes the human being a witness against the self despite offered excuses.
Connects accumulated earning with a covering over hearts, a mechanism of formed moral perception.
Links chosen deviation with hearts subsequently turned aside, preserving a reciprocal trajectory of inner state and course.
Introduces the tested human as hearing and seeing before the divergent response stated in 76:3.
Places differing belief within created human existence under divine sight of what people do.
Provides the fitrah frame for a divinely established human orientation, a broad counterpart to شاكلة.
